newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit in range, seen rising on falling dlr/yen.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit in range, seen rising on falling dlr/yen.

text.p: The ringgit held on to early gains and was trading in a narrow range in late Kuala Lumpur, dealers said on Thursday.
They said the falling dollar/yen was expected to give fresh momentum to the ringgit, though gains are expected to be limited due to a strong resistance at 2.5180 a dollar level.
"Ringgit is just tracking dollar/majors. It has no momentum of its own," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
He said if the trend continued, dollar/ringgit could test 2.5180 either late on Thursday or early Friday. At 0800 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5215/25 a dollar against 2.5240/50.
Dealers said the ringgit was under pressure to retreat at every small recovery in dollar/yen.
Speculators and funds out of Hong Kong were dumping the dollar after its sharp decline in early Tokyo.
"This triggered some buying from Singapore-based parties. One U.S. bank was aggressively buying (dollar/ringgit)," said a dealer with another U.S. bank in Singapore.

Dealers said interest rate swaps softened due to the rise of the ringgit. "There is no arbitrage opportunity right now, so few are focusing on swaps," a dealer with a large Malaysian bank said. -- Madhav Reddy (603-230 8911)
